3. Data Flow: From Building Listing to Survey Solutions Assignment

Source: vignettes/data-flow-and-suso-assignment.Rmd
data-flow-and-suso-assignment.Rmd

End-to-End Architecture

susolisting bridges spatial sampling and CAPI field operations by connecting first-stage Enumeration Area (EA) boundary shapefiles, desk enumeration on high-resolution satellite imagery, second-stage spatially balanced sampling (spsurvey), and automated Survey Solutions assignment creation (SurveySolutionsAPIv2).

End-to-end data flow across the four stages of the susolisting workflow.

Stage-by-Stage Data Pipeline

Stage 1: Spatial Boundary Input & Satellite Map Initialization

Component Function / Object Input Format Output / State
Provider Resolution resolve_map_provider() provider = "google" or "vantor" ("maxar") Sets options(susolisting.provider = ...)
Coverage Grid Resolution resolve_n_grid() n_grid = 10L (default 10 x 10 grid) Sets options(susolisting.n_grid = ...)
Boundary Upload shapeLoad2() .zip containing .shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj sf polygon object transformed to EPSG:4326 (boundaryFile())
Cluster Identifier areaIDs() User-selected column (input$area_id) Validated vector of unique EA identifiers
Map Canvas googleway::google_map() or leaflet::leaflet() + vantorr::add_vantor_basemap() Google API key or Vantor WMTS/WMS API key Interactive satellite map zoomed to lgaSel()

Stage 2: Building Enumeration, Spatial Coverage Check & Incremental .fst Persistence

As an enumerator clicks building rooftops inside the active EA boundary (lgaSel()), the browser’s custom drawing handler (suso_drawing_js()) places a marker and emits input$detailSampMap_markercomplete:

  1. In-Memory Collector (pointsCollectorGoogle()): Accumulates newly placed markers for the active Enumeration Area in a data.table:

    long (numeric) | lat (numeric) | area_id (character)

  2. Spatial Grid Coverage Check (calculate_polygon_coverage()): Whenever the enumerator clicks Next (input$loadNextEA) or Download Locations (input$downloadActivate), persist_area_points() evaluates the spatial distribution of saved points across the active EA polygon (lgaSel()):

    • Both the polygon and the collected building coordinates are projected into planar UTM meters via project_to_utm().
    • An n_grid x n_grid regular spatial grid (10 x 10 cells by default, configured via n_grid) is generated over the polygon with sf::st_make_grid() and filtered to the GpolygonG_{\text{polygon}} grid cells that intersect the polygon interior (sf::st_intersects()).
    • The coverage percentage is computed from the number of polygon grid cells GoccupiedG_{\text{occupied}} that contain at least one listed building: Coverage (%)=GoccupiedGpolygon×100\text{Coverage (\%)} = \frac{G_{\text{occupied}}}{G_{\text{polygon}}} \times 100
    • Polygons with < 20% spatial coverage are flagged (coverage_status = "LOW", low_coverage = TRUE), triggering a warning notification in the UI and highlighting the cluster status in bold red in the sidebar AreaSummary table (ID, Listed Units, Coverage, Status).

  3. On-Disk Persistence (persist_area_points()): The merged building coordinates and coverage attributes (long, lat, area_id, coverage_pct, coverage_status) are written to disk in fast binary .fst format:

    <app_download_dir>/<sanitized_user>_<shapefile_name>/area_<clean_id>.fst

  4. Individual Archive Export (BuildingFrame-<timestamp>.zip): When downloaded in local mode, the .fst files are combined into AreaswithMarker-<timestamp>.csv alongside the polygon attribute table AllAreas-<timestamp>.csv.

Stage 3: Multi-Enumerator Frame Compilation & Second-Stage Sampling

In administrator mode (modal_adminspsample_server() and modal_spsample2stage_server()):

  1. Frame Compilation & Coverage Backfilling (dt_frame() & summarize_cluster_coverage()): All area_*.fst files across all <user>_<shapefile> folders are read and bound via data.table::rbindlist(..., idcol = "ea", fill = TRUE), sorted by c("ea", "long", "lat"). If any legacy .fst files lack coverage_pct, calculate_polygon_coverage(polygon_sf = NULL, ...) automatically backfills coverage using a buffered convex hull of the cluster’s points. Cluster-level coverage is aggregated via summarize_cluster_coverage() and displayed in the Frame Summary table (Average Area Coverage (%) and Low-Coverage Segments (<20%)).
  2. Dynamic UTM Projection (project_to_utm()): Before calling spsurvey, the WGS84 point frame is converted to an sf object and dynamically projected into the appropriate Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) zone in meters: Zone=⌊λ‾+1806⌋+1\text{Zone} = \left\lfloor \frac{\bar{\lambda} + 180}{6} \right\rfloor + 1 producing EPSG:326xx (Northern Hemisphere) or EPSG:327xx (Southern Hemisphere). This ensures that spatial balance and minimum distance constraints (mindis in meters) are computed on planar metric coordinates.
  3. Sample Selection (spsurvey::grts() / spsurvey::irs()): For each stratum hh (cluster), the target sample size is capped at the cluster’s building count (nh=min(nsample,Nh)n_h = \min(n_{\text{sample}}, N_h)). The resulting sites_base sf object is transformed back to EPSG:4326 (sampleData()), containing:
    • siteID: Unique sampled unit identifier generated by spsurvey
    • ea and area_id: Cluster identifiers
    • lon_WGS84, lat_WGS84: Geographic coordinates in decimal degrees
    • wgt: Design weight (Nh/nhN_h / n_h)
  4. Automated Word Sampling Report (sampling_report_server() / build_sampling_report_docx()): Alongside the zipped CSV sample download, the sampling module provides a dedicated officer-powered reporting module (R/shiny_sampling_report_module.R) that generates a World Bank Group-styled .docx report documenting the frame, spatial grid coverage diagnostics and low-coverage cluster alerts, the spatial sampling process and parameters, and the resulting cluster-level sample and coverage tables.

Stage 4: Survey Solutions Variable Mapping & Supervisor Assignment

In the SuSo tab (mapadminSRV_st2()), the sampled building units are linked directly to a live Survey Solutions server via SurveySolutionsAPIv2:

Survey Solutions assignment interface showing API connection status, cover-page variable mapping, and supervisor team assignment tables.

  1. Server Authentication & Questionnaire Structure:
    • SurveySolutionsAPIv2::suso_set_key() and SurveySolutionsAPIv2::suso_PwCheck() validate the server URL, workspace, API user, and password.
    • SurveySolutionsAPIv2::suso_getQuestDetails() retrieves the list of imported questionnaires. Selecting a questionnaire fetches its JSON structure (operation.type = "structure") and extracts all cover-page identifying variables (Featured == TRUE):
      • Non-GPS variables (IDVARS()) for preloading cluster/building IDs.
      • The featured GpsCoordinateQuestion variable (GPSVAR()) for preloading building coordinates.
  2. Interactive Variable Mapping (suso_map_idSRV()):
    • Clicking Select Variables opens a modal where the administrator maps sample columns (e.g., ea, area_id, siteID) to the corresponding Survey Solutions cover-page variables (e.g., id_ea, id_cluster, id_building).
    • The lon_WGS84 and lat_WGS84 columns are automatically formatted into Survey Solutions’ GPS preload string ("<lat>$<lon>" rounded to 8 decimal places) and bound to GPSVAR().
  3. Supervisor Team Dispatch (suso_createASS()):
    • The administrator selects one or more sampled buildings (or clusters) in the left table (assignTable), selects a field supervisor in the right table (teamTable, populated via SurveySolutionsAPIv2::suso_getSV()), and clicks Create Assignments.
    • susolisting iterates over the selected units and calls SurveySolutionsAPIv2::suso_createASS() for each sampled building, assigning it to ResponsibleName with preloaded ID and GPS coordinates.
    • The Assignment Overview table in the left sidebar logs the number of assignments created per team and provides a confirmation-protected Reset button.
